findings.sourceEvidence: the sale or issuance of the Capital Stock of (i) any Subsidiary to the Parent Borrower or any Subsidiary Guarantor, (ii) any Subsidiary (other than a Subsidiary Guarantor) to any Subsidiary Guarantor and (iii) any Subsidiary that is not a Loan Party to any other Subsidiary;
findings.verifierReasoning: The entire operative content of §7.5(d) is the identity of the subsidiary whose Capital Stock is sold/issued and the identity of the permitted transferee. The source does not create a free-standing unconditional permission. By representing the gate as UNSUPPORTED and recording no conditions or exceptions, the IR presents each carve-out as an ungated unlimited capacity. A consumer relying on the structured IR could conclude, for example, that §7.5(d)(i) permits the sale or issuance of any Subsidiary's Capital Stock to any Person, which the source does not say. This materially overstates the scope of the permission.

findings.sourceEvidence: any Subsidiary (other than a Subsidiary Guarantor) to any Subsidiary Guarantor
findings.verifierReasoning: In the source clause (ii), the parenthetical '(other than a Subsidiary Guarantor)' qualifies only the transferor/issuer subsidiary. The transferee is affirmatively required to be a Subsidiary Guarantor. The IR's top-level entityScopeExcluded of GUARANTOR_RS excludes the very class of counterparty the source requires and permits. A reviewer using the IR could wrongly conclude that a sale/issuance of a non-guarantor Subsidiary's Capital Stock to a Subsidiary Guarantor is outside this exception, when it is exactly what the source permits.

findings.sourceEvidence: any Subsidiary that is not a Loan Party to any other Subsidiary
findings.verifierReasoning: The source clause (iii) qualifies only the transferor/issuer subsidiary ('any Subsidiary that is not a Loan Party'); the transferee is unqualified 'any other Subsidiary', which includes Subsidiaries that are Loan Parties. The IR excludes all LOAN_PARTY entities from the rule's scope, thereby excluding a permitted transferee. This is particularly clear by contrast with §7.5(n), where the drafters expressly added 'that is not a Loan Party' to the transferee when they intended that restriction. The IR's exclusion reverses part of the source's scope.

findings.proposedIrEvidence: action: "OTHER" for each of the three rules
findings.sourceEvidence: the sale or issuance of the Capital Stock of (i) any Subsidiary ...
findings.verifierReasoning: The only act that §7.5(d) permits is the 'sale or issuance of the Capital Stock' of a Subsidiary. Encoding the action as 'OTHER' means the structured IR does not convey what activity is being permitted. A downstream compliance check cannot distinguish a permitted capital-stock disposition under this exception from some unrelated disposition that would remain subject to the Section 7.5 prohibition. This is a material loss of operative content.
